title: Exile
lead: Exile is the loss of the land, foretold in the covenant curses (Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28), carried out by Assyria (722 BC) and Babylon (586 BC), and answered by promises of return. It became one of the Bible's central pictures of judgment and hope.

sections.b: The story begins with exile from Eden (Genesis 3:23–24). Leviticus 26:33–45 and Deuteronomy 28:64–68 warn that a faithless Israel will be scattered, and promise that God will remember his covenant. Assyria deports the northern tribes (2 Kings 17:6, 23), and Babylon takes Judah (2 Kings 25:11). Jeremiah sets seventy years (Jeremiah 29:10), Ezekiel sees God's glory leave and return (Ezekiel 10; Ezekiel 43), and Isaiah 40 begins "Comfort, comfort my people." Cyrus lets the exiles return (Ezra 1). Daniel and Nehemiah confess the sins of the fathers as Leviticus 26:40 foresaw (Daniel 9; Nehemiah 9). In the New Testament, Peter writes to believers as "exiles" (1 Peter 1:1), and some scholars, such as N. T. Wright, argue that many Jews of Jesus' day saw the exile as not yet truly over.
